translation.title: Diclofenac Sodium Plaster
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for pain relief and anti-inflammation in degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis and tenosynovitis, peritendinitis, epicondylitis of the humerus (tennis elbow, etc.), muscle pain (muscular and myofascial pain, low back pain, etc.), and post-traumatic swelling and pain.
translation.usage: Adults aged 15 and older: apply 1 plaster to the affected area once a day.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you have experienced hypersensitivity to it, if you have or have had asthma or hypersensitivity reactions caused by aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, if you are a child under 15, in the third trimester of pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have bronchial asthma, if it is used for inflammation accompanied by infection or for chronic conditions (such as degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis)), if you are in the first or second trimester of pregnancy, having difficulty conceiving or undergoing fertility testing, or elderly. Do not apply to the eyes, mucous membranes, damaged skin, or areas with eczema or rash. Do not use with an occlusive dressing. While using this medicine, do not apply other diclofenac products or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs topically or use them orally. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are using new-quinolone antibacterials (enoxacin, etc.), loop diuretics (furosemide, etc.), thiazide diuretics, drugs that interfere with blood clotting (warfarin, etc.), antiplatelet agents (aspirin, etc.), selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors. Sometimes dermatitis, itching, redness, roughness, or irritation may occur; applying to damaged skin may cause temporary irritation or a tingling sensation. Photosensitivity reactions, swelling, skin peeling, eczema, dry skin, rarely blistering or pigmentation, and very rarely hypersensitivity reactions, angioneurotic edema, or asthma may occur. If any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. If serious skin reactions such as exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, or toxic epidermal necrolysis, or serious gastrointestinal reactions including bleeding, ulcer, or perforation of the stomach or intestine occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Store at room temperature away from moisture and light, and keep out of reach of children.
